about: Would You Rather (Live) for CS Quest unit 6 (plan section 7). The dilemmas themselves live in the official game's bank (scripts/data/would-you-rather/en.json, topics tech and online, translated in the 11 other data files); this file adds what the WYR format has no room for: the teacher's prompt after each reveal and the CSTA 2017 ids each dilemma practices. Unscored: the reveal is the class split plus the all-time split. The lesson materialiser links these starters from the Would You Rather (live) step; the prompts print with the lesson.

items.prompt: Who is helped? What would the robot need to sense?
Which one changed how people live more?
Who gains, who loses a job, who do you trust?
How has technology changed learning? What did it not change?
What data does each collect? Who should see it?
What did people do before video calls?
What is the tradeoff between handy and private?
How does the free game make money?
Which would change your day more? Why?
What can a robot not do well here?
What skill might you lose? What do you gain?
How might this change jobs for translators?
Which helps more people?
Who needs to hear the street? Who needs quiet?
What job changes? What is nicer?
What does the fridge know about you?
What is better on each? Who is left out by each?
Which jobs change? Which get safer?
Who should get the credit for a computer-made song?
Which skills from this program does each need?
What could go right? What could go wrong?
Who else might see them later?
What does a stranger learn from a real name?
What are you paying with?
What is the middle path?
Who may know your passphrase?
What happens when the tablet breaks?
What does credit do for the artist?
Who might comment? Who moderates?
Is anything online ever really gone?

both: What could go wrong with A? With B?

2.wyr-tech: Who is helped, who is hurt, what job changes?
2.wyr-online: What is public, what is private, who else could see it?

scaffold.defend: Defend on every other reveal: one student for A, one for B, thirty seconds each.
scaffold.note: The tech set keeps 20 dilemmas; the lesson hosts 8 at 20 seconds (CA-9). Teachers may host 10 on a block day.
